systems.claim_boundary: Two nuclear-tree treatments are one radiation; profile intervals are conditional on fixed trees.
Tree/source-coding sensitivities are correlated settings within one radiation; hue signal does not identify ecological or molecular cause.
Two executed ML reconstruction sets are sensitivities within one radiation; organ signal does not identify ecological or molecular cause.
Posterior trees are correlated uncertainty within one radiation. Historical ISTA MD5 drift remains explicit; this test does not estimate ancestry or transition rates.

direction_rule.interpretation: The three source-to-tree Mk reanalyses do not yield a shared supported transition-rate direction. Antirrhineae is not added to this denominator because v0.1 there is a nested-state organization test, not a transition-rate reanalysis.

ancestry_direction_decoupling.interpretation: A robust WHITE ancestral state can coexist with failure to support directional rate asymmetry.

hierarchical_fine_state_rule.candidate_rule: Coarse ancestral/display or pigment state constrains the evolutionary state space without fixing a universal transition direction; phylogenetic organization persists at finer hue, floral-organ, or pigment-class levels after conditioning on the coarse state.
hierarchical_fine_state_rule.next_gate: Attempt falsification in an additional independent nested-state radiation and test whether the same hierarchy aligns with molecular regulatory-module reuse rather than only visible-state organization.

claim_boundary: Direction, ancestry and nested-state tests have different admissible denominators. Sensitivity trees, posterior trees, source codings and reconstruction repeats are not counted as independent radiations. Hydrangea lacks a comparable nested fine-state ingroup test in its current WHITE/RED coding.
